positions.as_written: Recognise it as a thin vertically oriented fleck parallel to the tibial cortex.
Assess the cruciate deliberately once it is seen, because the association is the point.
Assess the posterolateral and anterolateral structures, which is where the fragment came from.
Proceed to a magnetic resonance study, since the radiograph has done its job by raising the question.
The associated posterolateral corner must be assessed separately, since the two are not the same injury.
Whether an extra-articular augmentation should be added to a cruciate reconstruction is an active question, and this fragment is one of the inputs rather than an answer.
